checks.finding: The supplied source gives native token weights 1/4 and fold masses 1/2. On span(e0,e1), log(E0)=cI+k sigma_x with the stated k. A two-token donor has zero construction aggregate, covariance b sigma_z and scale sqrt(1+2b^2). Exponentiation gives recipient weight difference h(a(b)). The global effect trace, exp(c), and contributions from the unused six dimensions cancel in recipient normalization.

Each recipient contributes its native mass 1/2 times its amplitude times the donor-induced weight difference, giving equation (1). Coherent four-token construction doubles the covariance to 2b sigma_z and gives scale sqrt(1+8b^2), yielding R(b) without an additional factor. Opposite full-fold amplitudes cancel the construction operator, restore native weights, and give full(b,-b)=0.

Sharing each fold's sign across all 39 distractors preserves independence of the two complete fold error vectors and their conditional zero means. The distractor logits are exactly F(t), xi*zeta*F(t), and either R(t) or zero for self, cross, and full respectively. Because all distractor logits coincide within each draw, equation (3) is the exact expected per-draw CE. Strict monotonicity of L proves cross risk is strictly below self risk for every s,t>0.

With q=tanh(k)/k, h(x)=qx+O(x^3), F(b)=qb^2+O(b^4), and R(b)=2qb^2+O(b^4). Using L'(0)=39/40 gives exactly the three stated risk expansions. For each fixed 1<r<sqrt(2), the leading coefficients satisfy -1<r^2-2<0<r^2-1, proving cross<full<native<self for sufficiently small positive s. No explicit finite threshold is established or needed.

The independent zero-mean amplitude errors produce observed amplitudes 0 or 2s. Cross logits are zero unless both folds are active, when they equal F(2s). Self logits are zero, F(2s)/2, or F(2s) according to the number of active folds. Thus self strictly improves true-class CE on the one-active event of probability 1/2, proving the expected-risk reversal. The expected cross logit is F(2s)/4.

The stated expression for g(b)/b is correct. Its first positive factor strictly decreases; its second positive factor strictly decreases because T(b) increases and tanh(T)/T strictly decreases for T>0. Consequently g(2s)<2g(s), hence F(2s)/4<F(s). For ell(z)=log(1+39 exp(-z)), strict convexity and strict decrease give E ell(z_cross)>ell(E z_cross)>ell(F(s)). Independence also justifies replacing recipient noise by its zero conditional mean on each noisy-donor route, but not replacing donor construction by clean construction.

The witnesses establish opposite strict expected-CE comparisons for the same source-interface maps under two explicit synthetic laws, including a positive region beating the full and native controls. They establish neither end-to-end feature/circuit reachability nor actual task benefit, empirical noise structure, numerical execution, novelty, quantum necessity, or L5.

risks: The results are exact-arithmetic deductions from the supplied source text; floating-point behavior and provenance hashes were not independently tested.
Utilities and states are stipulated at the measured interface; simultaneous realization by the original shared neural parameters is unproved.
The synthetic dependence structure is essential to these witnesses and is not an identified real-data noise model.
The positive-region threshold is existential, and the asymptotic result does not certify a numerically resolvable advantage at any specified signal size.
The negative witness compares self and cross; it does not establish a complete ordering involving full and native.
